The Time Service module shall use the GPT driver service Gpt_GetPredefTimerValue with the related resolution and width of the timers to get the current time value for the desired timer instance.
The "1us16bit" functions shall use the Timer GPT_PREDEF_TIMER_1US_16BIT as time base if a time base is needed.
The "1us24bit" functions shall use the Timer GPT_PREDEF_TIMER_1US_24BIT as time base if a time base is needed.
The "1us32bit" functions shall use the Timer GPT_PREDEF_TIMER_1US_32BIT as time base if a time base is needed.
The "100us32bit" functions shall use the Timer GPT_PREDEF_TIMER_100US_32BIT as time base if a time base is needed.
The Tm_ResetTimer function shall reset the provided timer instance. This means, the reference time of the timer instance shall be set to the current time of the related GPT Predef Timer.
The ResetTimer functions shall be reentrant, if the timer instances used in concurrent calls are different.

If development error detection for the Time Service module is enabled: If the parameter timerId is not a valid timer instance, the Tm_ResetTimer functions shall raise the development error TM_E_PARAM_VALUE .
The Tm_GetTimeSpan function shall calculate and deliver the time difference between the current time and the reference time of the timer instance.
The Tm_GetTimeSpan function shall perform proper wrap-around handling at subtraction (current time - reference time), if value of current time is less than value of reference time.
The GetTimeSpan functions shall be fully reentrant, this means even for the same timer instance.

If development error detection for the Time Service module is enabled: If the pointer parameter (timeSpan) is a null pointer, the Tm_GetTimeSpan functions shall raise the development error TM_E_PARAM_POINTER .
The Tm_ShiftTimer function shall shift the reference time of the timer instance. This means, the provided timer value shall be added to the reference time of the timer instance.
The Tm_ShiftTimer function shall perform proper wrap-around handling at adding (reference time + TimeValue), if the sum is greater than the maximum value of the timer.
The ShiftTimer functions with range 24bit shall limit the value of the parameter TimeValue to 0xFFFFFF .

If development error detection for the Time Service module is enabled: If the value of the parameter timeValue is greater than the maximum allowed of the base GPT predef timer ( 0xFFFFFF for 24bit timers and 0xFFFF for 16bit timers), the Tm_ShiftTimer functions shall raise the development error TM_E_PARAM_VALUE .
The ShiftTimer functions shall be reentrant, if the timer instances used in concurrent calls are different.
If development error detection for the Time Service module is enabled: If the timerId is not a valid timer instance, the Tm_ShiftTimer functions shall raise the development error TM_E_PARAM_VALUE .
The Tm_SyncTimer function shall synchronize two timer instances. This means, the reference time of the destination timer instance shall be set to the reference time of the source timer instance.
The SyncTime functions shall be reentrant, if the timer instances used in concurrent calls are different.
If development error detection for the Time Service module is enabled: If a parameter is not a valid timer instance, the Tm_SyncTimer functions shall raise the development error TM_E_PARAM_VALUE .
The Tm_BusyWait1us function shall perform busy waiting for the minimum time passed by the parameter WaitingTimeMin .
The Tm_BusyWait1us function shall not disable the interrupts. This means the real waiting time may be greater than the desired waiting time.
The Tm_BusyWait1us function shall guarantee the minimum waiting. This means, n+1 ticks must be observed to ensure that an interval of at least n ticks have passed.
The BusyWait functions shall be reentrant.
For each Predef Timer enabled by configuration the following set of API services shall be available: ResetTimer , GetTimeSpan , ShiftTimer , SyncTimer .
For each Predef Timer with tick duration 1  s enabled by configuration the API service BusyWait shall be available.

Each instance of ara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer shall independently monitor for a synchronization timeout by measuring the time since that last update and a specified timeout duration in syncLossTimeout.
In case of a monitored timeout (refer [SWS_TS_00030]) the ara::tsync::SynchronizationStatus shall be set to kTimeOut.
If the update of the Time Base is successful and the SYNC_TO_GATEWAY bit is NOT set, the ara::tsync::SynchronizationStatus shall be set to kSynchronized.
The TBR shall perform Rate Correction measurements to determine its rate deviation if ara::tsync::SynchronizationStatus is set to kSynchronized.

The TBR shall perform Rate Correction measurements continuously. The end of a measurement marks the start of the next measurement. The start and end of measurements is always triggered by (and aligned to) the reception of time values for Synchronized.
During runtime, the Synchronized TBR shall determine the timespan of a Rate Correction measurement on the basis of clock ara::core::SteadyClock.
The TBR shall perform as many simultaneous Rate Correction measurements as configured by the parameter ’GlobalTimeCorrectionProps.rateCorrectionsPerMeasurementDuration’.

Simultaneous Rate Correction measurements shall be started with a defined offset (ton) to yield Rate Corrections evenly distributed over the measurement duration. At the end of the Rate Correction measurement, the Synchronized TBR shall take the time-snapshots TGStop and TVStop in the scope TSP.
